ai.description: Anandan’s Day Gecko reaches 35 mm SVL. It is brownish-grey with a distinct pale vertebral stripe and dark lateral spots. Key features include granular dorsal scales and a prominent yellow tail tip.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cnemaspis anandani* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous series of enlarged, spine-like tubercles along the flanks, which are absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: Anandan’s Day Gecko inhabits moist deciduous forests in the Western Ghats, typically found on large granite boulders at elevations between 300 and 600 meters.
ai.behavior: Anandan’s Day Gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects on rock surfaces within its restricted habitat in the Western Ghats.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cnemaspis anandani* is oviparous, laying a single hard-shelled egg per clutch. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cnemaspis anandani* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically found in the Wayanad district of Kerala at elevations between 800 and 1,100 meters.
